pageCache.pageTitle: Thomas’s College | Senior School in Richmond
pageCache.text:
A new co-educational day and weekly boarding school in Richmond for young people aged 11 to 18.
A Warm Welcome
An exceptional educational experience enabling students to achieve outstanding academic outcomes and build the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed in the world.
My child feels accepted and that they belong, for me that sense of belonging is foundational, particularly in adolescence.
Will le Fleming
Will is passionate about educational innovation to focus what schools do on the joy of learning and to combine academic excellence and success with happiness, confidence, creativity and hope for the future.
Radical Innovation, Traditional Excellence
Our educational approach is always both/and: outstanding outcomes and the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed – both excellence and joy.
Our Senior School therefore combines London’s leading programme of education reform and the traditional excellence that leads to established success.
Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Thomas’s College. Visit us for an Open Day, make an enquiry or contact our Admissions team. We are here to support your family through every stage of our admissions process and look forward to meeting you.
Hear from our Community
As part of our radical and innovative approach, we have redefined the journey through school into three distinct phases: Fourth Form, Fifth Form and Sixth Form. Each phase of school life has its own character. Academic rigour is a given, but so is joy. Joy is in every day, every week and throughout the year.
The first ever generation of Thomas’s College students celebrate their GCSE results.

Master’s Welcome
WELCOME TO THOMAS’S COLLEGE
Master’s Welcome
I am delighted you are considering Thomas’s College. You will be at the forefront of our innovative and ground-breaking education and among the first to make use of our state-of-the-art classrooms, galleries, studios and superb local sports facilities.
Why Thomas’s College? Because we combine decades of excellence in London education with an innovative and radical approach to what matters most: education, happiness and future success.
For over 50 years Thomas’s schools have been built on four pillars: kindness, breadth of experience, self-knowledge and a joyful approach to outstanding academic success. Thomas’s College shares these principles and provides an outstanding education allowing young people to secure the traditional qualifications they need for world-class outcomes.
However, as a brand-new Senior School, we provide an education built for the future. Our radical innovations place students at the centre of their own learning and allow families to create their own path through the curriculum. The best teaching methods, new forms of assessment alongside the most respected qualifications, and inventive principles such as our unique three-year Sixth Form, unlock a diversity of excellence that allows every individual to thrive on their own terms.
Outstanding teaching in small classes, remarkable co-curricular opportunity in art, dance, music, design, drama, sport and much more, and a pastoral system that provides the highest standards of care – these are all a given. On top of that we offer a family atmosphere, full of heart, and the passion and drive of an entrepreneurial start-up environment – one that is backed by the Thomas’s history and heritage. It is a combination that we believe will bring our students benefits, in terms of their success, happiness and values, that will last lifelong.
I hope you will join me and my dedicated staff at Thomas’s College. We’re setting out to be the leading pioneers and innovators in London, with a genuinely unique offer designed to open up a lifetime of adventure, exploration and fulfilment for our students. We look forward to welcoming you.
Will le Fleming,Founding Master

Vision and Values
Our Vision
Our vision is that every Thomas’s pupil flourishes as a compassionate contributor to society and a courageous shaper of the future.
To realise this vision, we:
Together, these commitments create the Thomas’s culture of joyful excellence, in which our pupils achieve both outstanding academic outcomes and build the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed in the world.
‘Thank you for your patience, encouragement and commitment to helping each child reach their full potential. We are truly grateful to be part of such a caring and inspiring school community.’
Champion kindness, community and childhood
Our Values
Kindness centres all that we do: simply, we are kind to ourselves and we are kind to others. We are a supportive community of good friends who actively look out for one another and ensure everyone feels encouraged.
Courtesy is at the heart of how we treat others and how we act in school: we build a happier world by being unfailingly polite, considerate and mindful of the impact of our behaviour on others.
Compassion connects us all: it demands that we see the world through each other’s eyes, appreciate different perspectives, and treat everyone with care and consideration.
Scholarship sparks our curiosity: we learn to think independently, focus, and approach every new challenge with creative and critical thought and a sense of wonder.
Integrity guides our choices: it is the moral purpose that leads us to be completely honest, mean what we say, and do the right thing even when no one is watching.
Respect unites our school: we value ourselves, each other, and our environment, while proudly championing and celebrating the unique differences that make us who we are.
Perseverance turns challenges into triumphs: we cheerfully embrace hard work and patience, knowing that our minds grow stronger with effort and that setbacks are simply chances to learn.
Confidence is our quiet strength: an inner superpower, we believe in ourselves and celebrate who we are without boasting, giving us the bravery to face challenges and know that our voices truly matter.
Leadership unites courage and empathy: we lead by including everyone, taking responsibility for our actions, and use a voice that speaks up for what is right and fair for everyone.
Kindness is where we begin, and helping others is what we do: we show a true spirit of generosity by using our unique abilities, time and privileges to leave the world around us a kinder and better place.

About Us
A NEW APPROACH TO LONDON INDEPENDENT EDUCATION
About Thomas’s College
Thomas’s College is a beautiful brand-new co-educational day and weekly boarding school for young people aged between 11 and 18. The College is at the leading edge of innovation, the facilities are immaculate, the wonderful campus is historic: a delightful set of buildings within five acres of leafy gardens at the top of Richmond Hill.
The College is a wonderful place to live, learn and grow, and offers a wholly new approach to independent education that lives up to our magnificent setting.
Our offering has been built from our team’s experience in London’s top academic schools, from consultation with universities and employers, with parents, and with young people themselves. We’re redrawing how secondary education works in all sorts of vital ways.
Our students are ready for the world’s top destinations: but much more importantly, they are equipped with all they need to be happy, fulfilled and successful in a changing world.

Results and Destinations
Results and Destinations
Thomas’s College opened in September 2025. Our first GCSE results were received in August 2026 and our first set of A Level results will be available in August 2027.
Inaugural GCSE Results at Thomas’s College
The first ever generation of Thomas’s College students celebrate their GCSE results.
As a cohort they have achieved outstanding outcomes, with well over half of all grades at 9-7 (A* and A) and over a third of all grades in the A* (9-8) category. Their GCSE journey began at our previous senior school Thomas’s Putney Vale, where they completed Years 9 and 10, before joining Thomas’s College as our first Lower Sixth (Year 11). They embraced the transition with enthusiasm, and throughout their first year at the College have shown commitment and dedication. They are now looking forward to a diverse, creative and rigorous set of subjects and ambitions for A Level study and beyond.
There are many stories to celebrate. Lucas achieved a remarkable average point score of 8.9, with seven Grade 9s, and is going on to study Maths, Economics, Spanish and Geography. Niamh’s five Grade 9s support her continued study of Spanish, Psychology, Philosophy and Politics. Sam takes an average point score of 8.3 into his A Levels of Maths, Computer Science and Economics. Sujood’s grades, all at 7-9, lead her to Art, English Literature, Biology and Chemistry, while Anfisa takes her 8 and 9 in Maths and Art onto A Level study alongside Economics next year. The range of choice, from the 26 subjects we support, and the variety of intended future pathways among this cohort is wonderful and shows their success in finding the path that is right for them.
More than anything, however, we celebrate every student’s achievement in terms of their own personal best. It was not uncommon to see students achieving grades that were two, three or even four levels higher than their previously expected scores, thanks to inspirational teaching, 1:1 support and their own sense of purpose and sheer hard work. We were particularly delighted by the outstanding successes achieved by bursary students, including Ukrainian students supported by Thomas’s since the start of the conflict, whose remarkable outcomes are a testament to their determination to overcome challenges and build the futures they deserve. And we were thrilled by how well our Wesley House boarders did – thanks in part to the brilliant team ensuring the right mix of fun and focus in this crucial examination year. Vasi, for example, secured six Grade 8s and goes on to study Politics, English Literature, Spanish and Geography next year.
Our passion at Thomas’s is to support each individual to achieve to the utmost of their ability while developing the character, confidence and adaptability to succeed in the real world. Numbers and grades help open doors to future opportunity: but self-knowledge, inner strength and intellectual curiosity enable our students to make the most of all they go on to experience.
We’re hugely grateful for the tireless efforts of staff, not just during school terms but in running dedicated revision sessions across February half-term and Easter – their personal care and investment in the success of students have been inspiring. And we’re just so proud of everything our first ever group of Lower Sixths (Year 11s) have achieved. Along with the Middle Sixths (Year 12s) above them, they’ve been role models for the community and pioneers as we build a new way in London independent education: one that blends radical innovation and traditional excellence to help develop students who are ready for the changing world that awaits them. They’ve done brilliantly in their exams – but what matters most is that they are wonderful young people developing into adults ready to shape the future and contribute to society.
Will le FlemingMaster, Thomas’s College

Safeguarding
Safeguarding
Safeguarding and the wellbeing of our students will always be our highest priority.
Our pastoral care system is carefully designed to ensure that every young person is noticed and valued and their voices heard. We build in mentoring opportunities by creating small mixed-age groups of around 15 students, with Years 7 and 8 together, Years 9 and 10 together, and Years 11 to 13 together, learning from each other’s life experience. These groups are integrated with our House system, giving the opportunity for genuine inter-year friendships. You can find more detail about this on our Pastoral Care page.
Safeguarding goes far beyond pastoral care: it is at the heart of everything we do and the first consideration for every adult within the school community. We are alert and attentive, never take the safety of students for granted, and always keep their best interests in mind in every area of decision-making.
Please read our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy for further information.
Safeguarding Contacts
If you have a concern about a student at Thomas’s College, or if you observe behaviour that compromises a student’s safety, please contact our Safeguarding Team.
Designated Safeguarding Lead
collegesafeguarding@thomas-s.co.uk
Out of hours / school holidays
The school provides a roadmap for healthy relationships and instills a sense of family.
What is safeguarding?+
What is Child Protection?+
Child protection is part of the safeguarding process.
It focuses on protecting individual children identified as suffering or likely to suffer significant harm. This includes child protection procedures which detail how to respond to concerns about a child.
In England, the Department for Education is the government department responsible for all child protection policies. At a local level, local safeguarding partners such as the police, the local authority and designated safeguarding groups are in charge of managing any complaints or issues and ensuring that the principles of the Children Act are upheld.
Reporting Concerns+
What should I do if I am worried about a child?
If you have a safeguarding concern relating to a student at Thomas’s College, please contact our safeguarding team whose details are above.
If you believe a child is at immediate risk of harm, do not wait. Call 999 to reach the Police straight away. They will assess the situation and take immediate action to protect the child.
What if I am not sure whether my concern is serious?
Many people worry that they might be mistaken. However, safeguarding is always about putting the child first.
If something does not feel right, it is always better to share your concern. Speaking up may help protect a child and ensure they receive the support they need.
Who is responsible for safeguarding?
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. Teachers, school staff, families and the wider community all play an important role in keeping children safe.
At Thomas’s, all staff receive safeguarding training so they can recognise concerns and respond appropriately.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral Care
As you would expect in a school whose only true rule is ‘Be Kind’, our pastoral care is second to none. Every young person at Thomas’s College knows that they matter and that every other member of the community has their back.
Almost every teacher at the College is a tutor in the first lesson of every day: tutor time. Each tutor has a small, mixed age group of around 15 students. In the Fourth Form, tutor groups comprise Lower and Upper Fourth (Years 7-8); in the Fifth Form, Lower and Upper Fifth (Years 9-10); in the Sixth Form, Lower to Upper Sixth (Years 11-13).
Tutors lead discussions, share ideas, provide a listening ear, give advice, and represent the first link to home so that every family has a dedicated point of contact who knows their child well and is their champion in the school setting.
Teachers are getting to know my son as an individual, not just another face in a sea of blazers.
The Pastoral Team
Tutor groups are integrated with our House system, enabling genuine inter-year friendships. The tutor teams in Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Forms are led by dedicated Directors of Stage, and supported by Assistant Directors. They have oversight of student progress and wellbeing at each stage and are there to support families through more complex challenges. They come together as a pastoral team under the direction of the Head of Pastoral Care (DSL), who ensures that the student experience is at the forefront of the College’s Leadership Team.
Counselling and Medical Support
Counsellors are available to carry out one-to-one therapeutic work with students, to support their personal, social, emotional and related educational needs.
The College Medical Centre is staffed by two registered nurses. Our counselling and medical teams recognise that every student is different, and we use a holistic approach in planning student care, including their physical, emotional and psychological needs. The Medical Centre can provide first aid for minor injuries, first aid for mental health issues, emotional health and wellbeing as well as support students with their understanding of how to maintain their own physical and mental wellbeing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Radical Innovation and Traditional Excellence - Thomas's College

Radical Innovation and Traditional Excellence
THOMAS’S COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL APPROACH
Radical Innovation and Traditional Excellence
Our educational approach is always both/and: outstanding outcomes and the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed – both excellence and joy.
Our Senior School therefore combines London’s leading programme of education reform and the traditional excellence that leads to established success.
Radical Innovation
The education available at most schools is similar, and it is hard to determine what makes each school unique. That’s not the case at the College: our offer is bold, distinctive and unique. These are some of the things that make what we do special.
All Subjects Available To All Year Groups And Meaningful Choice+
Some schools offer a limited range of subjects and all schools restrict some of the most interesting disciplines, such as economics, politics and psychology, to Sixth Form students only. Not here.
Everyone studies everything in the Fourth Form (Years 7+8), including a course in PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics), and all students have meaningful choice from a wide range of alternatives going into Fifth Form (Year 9), a year earlier than most schools. They own their path through the curriculum: and the rewards are so much greater as a result.
Cognitive Psychology Taught From Age 11 Upwards+
Every student at Thomas’s is taught cognitive psychology as part of their personal development. This supports our four-dimensional approach to education, where self-understanding is as important as the traditional dimensions of knowledge, skills and character. If our young people understand themselves, their strengths and areas of growth, they will become hugely effective and capable across and beyond their studies.
Creativity And Freedom Of Thought+
Independent education in London is disfigured by the 11+/13+ system. Families compete in a system that tests a narrow form of intelligence and face strong incentives to subject their children to excessive tutoring. At all levels, this leads to narrowness: of experience, of aptitude, of creativity. We know the world’s best workplaces nurture different forms of intelligence and creativity.
Our commitment is to the same diversity of excellence and intelligence as the best workplaces. We are committed to a holistic selection process that focuses on personality, potential and imagination, not hoop-jumping and ineffective cognitive assessment.
Our Unique Three-Year Sixth Form+
Sixth Form – the top years at school – is the summit of secondary education, but it is too short: two years, much of which is taken up with university application and exams. Our Sixth Form, uniquely, starts earlier and lasts for three years.
The benefits are wide-ranging. All our public examination is concentrated into one phase of school life. Students start Sixth Form in Lower Sixth (Year 11), and complete GCSEs and equivalent exams at the end of the first year.
They then start on A Levels and equivalents. This period of their education is future-focused, treating them as grown-ups and helping them gain the qualifications they need. This protects the Fourth and Fifth Forms (Years 7-10), which focus on learning and growth, not the treadmill of exams.
Blue-Chip And Globally Recognised Qualifications Alongside A Brand-New Alternative+
This is our flagship educational reform and the heart of what makes Thomas’s different. All our students explore a wide range of academic disciplines with a sense of freedom and adventure from Lower Fourth (Year 7) to Upper Fifth (Year 10).
At the start of Lower Sixth (Year 11), they choose which of their subjects they will take to GCSE examinations at the end of the year, and which they will take to Thomas’s Qualifications (TQs) – our own new and innovative assessments encouraging real-world skills and abilities. Many schools are offering educational reform, and the majority of top London schools are exploring alternatives to GCSE. We are the only school, however, providing this reform on your terms, and putting families in charge of the balance between the new and the traditional.
Many of our young people will take GCSEs in the majority of their courses, with TQs giving them the chance to develop the skills they need in our changing world. Some may take more TQs to prepare them for entrepreneurial and creative pathways. Taking TQs is not about closing doors to traditional outcomes. It is about giving young people the confidence and abilities to stride through those doors, ready to make an impact on the world.
Thomas’s Qualifications+
TQs have already been recognised by UCAS, the UK university admissions system. We’re confident that the right mix of TQs will enhance the academic profile of every student in our school. TQs are mapped against the future skills our young people need. TQs help us put these skills at the heart of the experience for all students.
From Oxbridge to Entrepreneurship+

Traditional Excellence
Our ambition is to offer the best educational experiences available anywhere in London. Alongside our mission to reform and improve, this means offering the traditional excellence of the best London schools.
Leading With Values+
First and foremost, our education will always be based around one single priority that has guided us for over 50 years: Be Kind. This is a non-negotiable for us. If every child walks into school with excitement and assurance, knowing that every single member of the community, whether child or adult, has their back, they will be ready to achieve anything.

We’re determined to be the school that notices and values each young person as the individual they are. We have small pastoral groups of around 15 children and we make more time for those groups than other schools. The groups include children of different ages to help them learn from and guide each other.
True Co-Education+
In too many schools, especially those that began life as boys’ schools, there are systemic imbalances in the number of girls and boys. This can manifest further in a continued focus, for example on boys’ sport over girls’ sport. We believe in true co-education with all students learning to value each other as the individuals they are on equal terms.

A unique programme of personal development prepares students for the future and to help them become the people they mean to be. The programme includes:
Small group debate and discussion
Cognitive psychology, teaching the gift of self-understanding
Co-Curricular Passion And Opportunity+
Breadth of experience was one of the Thomas’s founding principles back in 1971. It remains a core focus of our educational offering across all traditional co-curricular disciplines and many more besides. Our co-curricular pages give a sense of the remarkable opportunities on offer.

We recognise the powerful role that technology plays both for good and for potential harm in our children’s lives. Our approach is phone-free to Sixth Form.
We want children to learn to navigate the digital world and to become critical thinkers regarding the benefits and harms of AI, so we issue them with iPads (and a choice of iPads or Macbooks in Middle and Upper Sixth) to support their learning. These devices are under close control, with no compulsory home use for younger students and parental controls over internet access, to help them manage and gain control of their use of screens.
The Best Of Traditional Education, Reinvigorated+
In everything we do, we are restless in seeking excellence: ensuring that everything we offer is considered and purposeful, aimed at supporting our goal of creating happy and optimistic young people.
There is an excitement to being part of something new.

Our Campus
THOMAS’S COLLEGE LOCATION
Our Campus
While we are at the leading edge of innovation, and our facilities are immaculate, our wonderful campus is historic: a delightful set of buildings within five acres of leafy gardens at the top of Richmond Hill.
Thomas’s College is a delightful place to live, learn and grow, and offers a wholly new approach to independent education that lives up to the magnificent setting.
Sport+
Our magnificent dedicated sports ground at Dukes Meadows in Chiswick, supports our programme of major sports, including rugby sevens, football, netball, hockey and cricket.
Students also have access to a superb Fitness Centre on site, make full use of our Sports Dome, and our location, accessing everything from horse-riding in Richmond Park to canoeing, kayaking and rowing on the Thames.
Dance+
Dance, across a plethora of styles, will always be a major element of Thomas’s life, encouraging self-expression and activity in equal measure. We have a fully equipped, dedicated Dance Studio for curriculum Dance and clubs.
Drama+
An ambitious programme of Drama opportunities exposes young people to acting, directing, design across set, lighting, sound and costume, choreography, devising and text. We also run a major partnership with Richmond’s world-class and renowned Orange Tree Theatre, supporting their sector-leading community programmes, and giving students access to professional experts and facilities. There are three on-site performance spaces at the College.
Music+
From performances in our lovely Recital Hall to the range of choirs, ensembles and orchestras across classical and contemporary music, Music is a huge part of life at the College. It is impossible to move around our campus without hearing singing or instrument practice. The Music and Drama departments also collaborate on regular musical performances.
Design and Engineering+
We are so fortunate to have a dedicated School for Design & Engineering, with practical workshops in a range of materials including metal, and a design studio and Mac Suite exploiting the potential of digital and computer-aided design.
Art+
The College has three principal art labs exploring media across 2D and 3D, with a hugely popular Pottery Room and kiln. Students produce breathtaking work in so many disciplines and continue to engage in art making throughout their time at school, no matter what their curriculum choices are.
Science+
Our labs are first class and state-of-the-art, with all facilities needed to support ambitious practical work at the heart of our Science curriculum.
Library+
We are blessed with a magnificent and historic Library, which students use for games of chess and literary puzzles, catching up on work and reading for pleasure.
Innovation+
The Old Chapel is an innovative space dedicated to thinking, making and creativity. A truly flexible environment, it is used for everything from art and design projects to performances, seminars, discussions and creative experimentation.
Computing+
Getting the balance right between technology and tradition is crucial to us. As part of this, students work with computers and technology, from network build to robotics, in a dedicated set of computing laboratories.
College Lawn+
The heart of our school. A gorgeous tree-filled expanse with students doing everything from playing volleyball, to games they’ve invented, to sitting in deckchairs or lying on the grass and watching the sky. On a sunny day, it is the nicest spot for break you could possibly imagine!

Radical Innovation and Traditional Excellence
THOMAS’S COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL APPROACH
Radical Innovation and Traditional Excellence
Our educational approach is always both/and: outstanding outcomes and the confidence, character and adaptability to succeed – both excellence and joy.
Our Senior School therefore combines London’s leading programme of education reform and the traditional excellence that leads to established success.
Radical Innovation
The education available at most schools is similar, and it is hard to determine what makes each school unique. That’s not the case at the College: our offer is bold, distinctive and unique. These are some of the things that make what we do special.
All Subjects Available To All Year Groups And Meaningful Choice+
Some schools offer a limited range of subjects and all schools restrict some of the most interesting disciplines, such as economics, politics and psychology, to Sixth Form students only. Not here.
Everyone studies everything in the Fourth Form (Years 7+8), including a course in PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics), and all students have meaningful choice from a wide range of alternatives going into Fifth Form (Year 9), a year earlier than most schools. They own their path through the curriculum: and the rewards are so much greater as a result.
Cognitive Psychology Taught From Age 11 Upwards+
Every student at Thomas’s is taught cognitive psychology as part of their personal development. This supports our four-dimensional approach to education, where self-understanding is as important as the traditional dimensions of knowledge, skills and character. If our young people understand themselves, their strengths and areas of growth, they will become hugely effective and capable across and beyond their studies.
Creativity And Freedom Of Thought+
Independent education in London is disfigured by the 11+/13+ system. Families compete in a system that tests a narrow form of intelligence and face strong incentives to subject their children to excessive tutoring. At all levels, this leads to narrowness: of experience, of aptitude, of creativity. We know the world’s best workplaces nurture different forms of intelligence and creativity.
Our commitment is to the same diversity of excellence and intelligence as the best workplaces. We are committed to a holistic selection process that focuses on personality, potential and imagination, not hoop-jumping and ineffective cognitive assessment.
Our Unique Three-Year Sixth Form+
Sixth Form – the top years at school – is the summit of secondary education, but it is too short: two years, much of which is taken up with university application and exams. Our Sixth Form, uniquely, starts earlier and lasts for three years.

Our Unique Curriculum
SIXTH FORM LEARNING RE-IMAGINED
Our Unique Curriculum
Lower Sixth (Year 11)
In our three-year Sixth Form, we consider Year 11 (Lower Sixth) part of the Sixth Form experience.
Students in Lower Sixth started their courses in Year 10 (Upper Fifth). However, at the start of Lower Sixth they face a significant choice: which of their courses do they want to take to GCSE? And which do they want to take to our unique Thomas’s Qualifications (TQs)?
Most students will want to keep their future study options open, and take at least eight GCSEs alongside two TQs. The most academically driven may take 10 GCSEs, and complete any TQs in addition to enhance their profile. Some students may already know their future path is more creative or entrepreneurial, and take more TQs and fewer GCSEs.
The course content is the same for GCSE and TQ, so there is no anxiety about learning new material. The TQ is simply a different, and more future-ready, method of assessing learning. Students pick one of four styles of TQ to suit their learning and their abilities:
More detail is in our Curriculum Guide.
For the typical student in Lower Sixth (not that there is any such thing at Thomas’s…), they will complete two TQs by Christmas. These TQs will complement their traditional GCSEs and help them stand out in their future applications. They will then have a little more time to study towards eight GCSEs in the summer.
Those doing all ten GCSEs will likely also complete at least one TQ, to help them stand out. Some students will complete two TQs by Christmas, and perhaps more by spring, allowing them to focus on fewer GCSEs in the summer and giving themselves more time and clearer focus to excel.
TQ Communication: assessment through oracy
Middle and Upper Sixth (Years 12-13)
There are three elements to our innovative curriculum for these crucial two years: major subjects, minor subjects and the Tutorial Programme. The mix of majors and minors is similar to the style of learning often found in US universities, guaranteeing remarkable breadth and academic rigour.
We continue to offer Thomas Qualifications (TQs) as alternatives to A and AS Level for some students, which means more breadth and more balance than any comparable school environment.
Above all, we integrate the skills and ways of thought students will need for high-level degree apprenticeships, the best college and university courses, and the entrepreneurial world of work, into our main curriculum – rather than asking young people to develop these skills in addition to core study. As an experience, our Middle and Upper Sixth curriculum is the best preparation available for university and other outcomes and avoids the narrowness that can limit a more standard UK Sixth Form experience.
Understanding the World
Create, Invent, Perform
FrenchGermanGreekLatinMandarinPoliticsSpanish
BiologyChemistryComputer ScienceMathsFurther MathsPhysical EducationPhysicsPsychology
Business StudiesClassical CivilisationEconomicsEnglish LiteratureGeographyHistoryTheology & Philosophy
ArtDesign & EngineeringDramaMusic
Major Subjects+
Students typically take three or four major subjects, almost always to A Level. Just like at GCSE, they can opt instead to finish a major course with a Thomas’s Qualification (TQ). It is less common at A Level, a more suitable option for creative or entrepreneurial students who are set on a less conventional path into their careers.
All students take the Thomas’s Project, which teaches high-level research and understanding. Students can choose their own subject, supported by a mentor, and they may choose to conclude the Project with either an EPQ (Extended Project Qualification – recognised and celebrated by UCAS and universities) or with one of our own TQs, which are more flexible and adaptable to students’ individual strengths.
Minor subjects+
There is a huge range of minor subjects available at Thomas’s College which provide unparalleled breadth in Middle Sixth (Year 12). Some are substantial, offering as many as six periods a week that may lead to an AS Level or TQ. Others may be as little as one period a week to allow for an interest to develop without the burden of a final assessment.
Our list of minor subjects changes every year but has included Astronomy, Creative Writing across a range of disciplines, Financial Literacy, Sports Leadership, Ancient and Modern Cultures, Woodwork, Jewellery Making, beginner language courses, and much more.
Tutorial Programme
Our Tutorial Programme (or Tutes) is a dedicated programme of personal development and future preparation. Tutes ensures variety and a depth of unique skill development. In an increasingly commoditised world, students need to not only develop the skills that make them happy, they also need to stand out and shine. Tutes is our approach to solving this problem.
The programme includes inspiring talks, lessons to prepare for life beyond school, careers and futures advice including one-on-one guidance on UK and international universities, and visits and information about the world of work, business and entrepreneurship.
See our Curriculum Guide for more information.
